artifact_set.rationale: Four rules because four genuinely different, unmissable glob sets exist and a merged index would blow the sub-200-line budget: java-quality and kotlin-quality split on **/*.java vs **/*.kt with disjoint depth (Kotlin's densest material — return-type widening breaking ABI, data classes in a public API, @JvmOverloads not preserving binary compatibility — has no Java analogue, and Java's — sealed+records+exhaustive switch, StructuredTaskScope, FFM restricted methods — has no Kotlin one); gradle-build and maven-build split because 0 of the 10 Gradle-tagged corpus repos with a pom.xml actually build with both, so a Maven-only adopter loading Gradle content gets pure noise. 27 depth files, one ID family each, routed by task never by topic name. Two skills, both procedures every adopter runs occasionally; the third candidate was standards wearing a procedure's clothes. Bundle jvm-essentials, members untagged.

conflicts_resolved: 1. Fat/shadow jars — resolved per consumer kind by measurement with zero counterexamples in 32 repos (pub): library = never shade (MUST); application = shading is the naive baseline, not the recommendation (nested/jlink/jpackage/Jib beat it); Gradle plugin = sanctioned (plugin-publish auto-applies shadow since 1.0.0); CLI = correct, with the merge-transformer and signature-exclusion taxonomy as MUSTs. Hypothesis 2 reshaped, not refuted

2. One jvm-quality vs separate java-quality and kotlin-quality — SEPARATE. Both globs are extension-shaped and unmissable, the depth is disjoint per canonical-java and canonical-kotlin, and a merged index lands near 300 lines against the catalog's observed 114-229. ~6 shared MUST rows duplicated bounded

3. Maven and Ant — OWN RULE (maven-build.md), not extra globs on gradle-build. Decided by shape's measurement that 0 of 10 Gradle+pom repos build with both; Ant folds in as one depth file because only apache/ant is genuinely Ant-built (1/32) and ant.importBuild has 0 real usages

4. buildSrc vs included build-logic — SHOULD build-logic, never call buildSrc a defect. Gradle's own Best Practices page is normative for direction; shape measured 10 repos on included builds against 9 flagships still on buildSrc, and Gradle documents two caveats (Settings plugins needing a separate build-logic-settings, very-large-subproject-count builds breaking Build Services)

5. Kotlin DSL vs Groovy for examples — Kotlin DSL throughout, with exactly two Groovy appearances (the apply plugin: → plugins {} migration row, and the gradlePlugin{plugins{}} id idiom where shape found two idioms with no dominant winner). Owner may override, Q4

6. Gradle plugin development — DEPTH FILE (gradle-build/plugin-authoring.md, GRADLE-PLUG), not a skill. Nearly all measured content is standards enforced while editing a *.gradle.kts file that gradle-build already globs; a skill would fire probabilistically where it must be constant

7. JUnit 6 vs 5 baseline — JUnit 5 is the baseline, 6 is the dated target. Release notes are normative (6.0.0, 2025-09-30, Java 17/Kotlin 2.2 floor, junit-platform-runner discontinued) but gates measured adoption at 4/32 and gradle/gradle pinning 5.12.2 for its own suite

8. JSpecify vs older nullness annotations — recommend JSpecify (MUST for the OCX SDK) but every row carries a coexistence note: four independent normative sources converge, while gates measured JSpecify 9/32, NullAway JSpecify-native mode 2/32, jsr305 13/32, checker-framework 8/32

9. Java gate of record — Error Prone + NullAway. Checkstyle is style-only with a named ruleset choice; SpotBugs earns a row only paired with find-sec-bugs; PMD is OUT (enforced 0/32; apache/maven declares it in pluginManagement with no executions, gradle/gradle implements the plugin without running it on itself)

10. detekt vs ktlint — BOTH, split by job. Settled from detekt's own source: detekt 2.0 renamed :detekt-formatting to :detekt-rules-ktlint-wrapper, an explicit admission it wraps ktlint. detekt for logic, ktlint (directly or via Spotless) for formatting, plus an explicit 'enabling both buys nothing' row

11. JaCoCo vs Kover — tool follows language (JaCoCo mis-reads Kotlin inline functions and synthetic accessors), but the load-bearing rule is report-vs-verify: a plugin application is not a floor, and the check must look for violationRules/jacocoTestCoverageVerification/minBound/<rules>

12. Coverage thresholds — two rules at different severities. Hard numeric floor enforced Linux-only for anything this program publishes (a pinned decision carried from ocx-sdk-python's fail_under=100); CONSIDER for adopters, since gates measured only 3/32 enforcing anything. Hypothesis 4 holds for lint, not coverage

13. Virtual threads vs reactive for the SDK — virtual threads, no reactive stack, and no StructuredTaskScope in shipped code while preview. The SDK's concurrency surface is a CLI-subprocess boundary (injectable factory seam, one-shot run, kill ladder, sysexit-to-exception mapping), not a request-per-thread server

14. Java-first vs Kotlin-first SDK — FRAMED, not decided (owner Q1), with three frame premises corrected first: the zero-dependency commitment is reachable in Java and not in idiomatic Kotlin; Kotlin has one converged ABI gate (BCV) where Java has none; a Kotlin-first public API needs explicitApi() plus five interop annotations plus a blocking wrapper for every suspend fun. Default if unanswered: Java-first with a Kotlin-friendly API

15. Structured concurrency preview count — the two scouts are BOTH right, not in conflict: JDK 26 ships the 6th preview (JEP 525), JDK 27 the 7th (JEP 533, GA 2026-09-15), finalisation targeted at JDK 28. Any row naming a concrete StructuredTaskScope call must carry its JDK number

16. Bazel-Java depth file — researched and drafted HERE, delivered to bazel-quality. Two rule sets both globbing BUILD.bazel would double-load, so no Bazel rule ships from this program; cfg §2.1 confirms the sibling has twelve finalized families and no Java one

17. Kotlin explicit API mode — default ON for anything this program publishes, SHOULD for adopters. kotlinlang's library guidance is unconditional; gates and shape both measured 5/32 against 15 Kotlin-library repos. The gap is 'recommended vs enabled', not a doc disagreement

18. Configuration cache 'on by default' — OVERTURNED. Gradle 9 makes it preferred with automatic graceful fallback; the default-execution-mode target moved from Gradle 10 to Gradle 11; shape measured 11/20 setting the property explicitly, and the check reads gradle.properties first (property 10/32 vs CLI flag 3/32)

19. Maven 4 GA — HOLD AT RC. prac asserts an October 2025 GA from mailing-list posts (argued, second-hand); shift fetched the 4.0.0-rc-6 release notes and flagged it contested; cmab quotes a page whose own header says it is updated 'until the 4.0.0 release'. Fetched release notes beat a summarised mailing list

20. Surefire 3.6.0 — both scouts right about different pages. The single-JUnit-Platform-provider change is documented and real; the released line is 3.6.0-M1, a milestone, per the core-plugin index. Any row about it carries the -M1 qualifier

21. Reproducible archives — Gradle 9 makes them reproducible BY DEFAULT (release notes, normative), which inverts pub's reading that kafka's preserveFileTimestamps=true / reproducibleFileOrder=false 'restates Gradle's defaults'. Kafka runs Gradle 9.7.1, so that block now actively opts OUT. The sharpest measured surprise in the map and a named wave-2 chase item (M-D-11)

22. Kotlin 2.2.0's date — resolved for ckt (2025-06-23) over shift's hedged 2026-03-27, which shift's own 2.3.0=2025-12 and 2.4.0=2026-06 dates make impossible. Both agree on the substance: -Xjvm-default is deprecated for a stable -jvm-default flag and jvmDefault DSL property, and the default value itself flipped to ENABLE in 2.2.0
frame_corrections: Configuration cache is 'preferred with automatic fallback' in Gradle 9, not on by default, and the default-execution-mode target moved from Gradle 10 to Gradle 11 (shift, cgrad, prac)
Maven 4.0 GA is not confirmed — latest verified is 4.0.0-rc-6; treat Maven 4 as release-candidate until a worker cites the GA note (shift)
JEPs 483, 491 and 493 shipped in JDK 24, not 25 — a full LTS cycle earlier than the frame's era list implies (shift)

Virtual threads no longer pin on synchronized/wait/notify as of JDK 24 (JEP 491), and jdk.tracePinnedThreads was REMOVED — three native-frame cases remain and the jdk.VirtualThreadPinned JFR event is now the only detector (failr, shift)

The isolated-projects property is org.gradle.isolated-projects; org.gradle.unsafe.isolated-projects is dead (0/32 versus 5/32) (shape)

The sibling Bazel set treats its twelve depth files as closed and lists rules_java/rules_kotlin as explicitly out of scope; handing over a java.md reopens a decision rather than filling a reserved slot (cfg)

Nothing in the catalog mentions the JVM, so the frame's duplication worry is moot; the conventions to match are structural — index plus depth, task-worded routing, language-prefixed families, verification cells that say what empty output means (cfg)

No repo derives its version from git tags via a plugin — axion-release, nebula-release, reckon and gradle-git-version are 0/32 each; versioning is a literal string in gradle.properties (14/32) or the POM (pub)

Sonatype measured 28% of ~37,000 LLM-assisted dependency upgrades as hallucinated packages or versions — this fleet's own agents are the population that statistic describes, which makes registry validation before a version bump a rule about us, not about adopters (failb)
owner_questions: Q1. Java-first or Kotlin-first for the OCX SDK? Java-first holds the zero-runtime-dependency commitment and keeps Kotlin consumers first-class via JSpecify's strict default; Kotlin-first gets one converged ABI gate (BCV) where Java has none, at the cost of the zero-dep claim and of solving suspend-across-the-Java-boundary on day one. DEFAULT: Java-first with a Kotlin-friendly API (JSpecify-annotated, no Optional parameters, no generics-into-varargs, no data-shaped public types)

Q2. What is the SDK's minimum JDK? Current LTS is 25, but Spring Boot 4 and JUnit 6 both hold at 17 and guava/grpc-java still ship Java 8 bytecode. DEFAULT: floor 17 (--release 17), toolchain 25, CI matrix 17/21/25. Raising to 21 buys virtual threads and pattern matching in the SDK's own code; 24 buys un-pinned synchronized

Q3. Does the OCX Gradle plugin support Gradle 8.x, or 9.x only? Hard constraint: a Kotlin-DSL plugin built with Gradle 9.x runs only on consumer Gradle >= 8.11. DEFAULT: declared floor 8.11, TestKit matrix of 8.11 / current 9.x / release-candidate, plus a configuration-cache leg

Q4. Kotlin DSL only in the rules' examples, or Groovy too? DEFAULT: Kotlin DSL for every example, with exactly two Groovy appearances (the apply plugin: → plugins {} migration row and the gradlePlugin{plugins{}} id idiom). Parallel Groovy snippets throughout roughly doubles the depth files' snippet budget

Q5. Does Maven get its own rule, and does Ant live on it? DEFAULT: yes — maven-build.md with **/pom.xml, **/.mvn/**, **/mvnw*, plus **/build.xml and the Ivy files, and Ant as one depth file. The alternative folds Maven onto gradle-build as a jvm-build rule, halving the artifact count and making every Maven-only adopter load Gradle content

Q6. Will bazel-quality accept a thirteenth depth file and a BZL-JAVA family? The sibling calls its twelve files finalized and lists rules_java/rules_kotlin explicitly out of scope, so this reopens a closed decision. DEFAULT: draft .agents/research/handoff/bazel-quality-java.md and offer it; if declined, the wave-3 output stays as research, BZL-JAVA is never allocated, and the M-X rows become backlog

Q7. What coverage floor does the OCX SDK enforce? ocx-sdk-python enforces fail_under=100 Linux-only; the JVM corpus's strictest is a Maven repo with a tiered rule (100% CLASS, 80% everything else) and only 3/32 enforce anything. DEFAULT: 90% line and branch, enforced Linux-only, with the number written in the config rather than a CI flag. Say if parity with Python's 100% matters more

Q8. Does docs-quality grow JVM rows, or is Dokka marked 'Not Studied'? Its per-language tested-example table has no Java or Kotlin row and its generator-wiring table has no shape for an output-only API-doc generator. DEFAULT: propose one row to tested-examples-by-language.md (neither language ships a doctest runner, so both fall to the generic subprocess harness) and add an explicit 'Not Studied' line for Dokka and Javadoc, matching the css-theming and docs-quality precedent

Settle what the configuration cache requires of build logic in Gradle 9.x, and
what "preferred with fallback" means in practice, so a rule can fail a diff
rather than describe a feature.

Pin down and write out as a table an agent can grep against: every disallowed
type at execution time (ClassLoader, Thread, Socket, Lock/Semaphore/CountDownLatch,
Project, Settings, SourceSet, Configuration), every configuration-time

the default since KSP 2.0.0 with KSP1 incompatible past Kotlin 2.3.0 or AGP 9.0,
and whether any commonly-used processor still lacks a KSP implementation and
forces kapt for one module; and what Dokka v1→v2 restructures (multi-module
aggregation, output directories, visibility settings) with K2 analysis stable
from 2.2.0.

DECIDE: (a) whether kapt may appear in a new module at all and what the rule
says to a project that still needs it; (b) whether -Wextra/extraWarnings is a
recommendation given it is still Experimental; (c) the Dokka version floor a
rule cites, and whether Dokka's output belongs in docs-quality's world or
outside it (M-Y-06 says the sibling's generator table has no shape for it).

wave3_staged.group_label: Java runtime safety: untrusted input and failure handling
wave3_staged.label: Every place attacker-controlled data picks a class or a path
wave3_staged.brief:
Write the Java security rows as a small set of shapes with named checks, not as a
survey of OWASP.

Fetch, primary only: cheatsheetseries.owasp.org Deserialization, XML External
Entity Prevention, Java Security, Input Validation and Cryptographic Storage
sheets; cmu-sei.github.io SEI CERT Oracle Java rules index (the IDS, FIO, SER
and SEC categories); github.com/FasterXML/jackson/wiki/Jackson-Polymorphic-Deserialization-CVE-Criteria
and advisory GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm (CVE-2026-54512/54513); snyk.io/research/zip-slip-vulnerability;
find-sec-bugs' rule list; oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/seccodeguide.html.

Pin down, each as a shape a reviewer can find: native deserialization of
untrusted data without an ObjectInputFilter; Jackson with global default typing
or a too-broad @JsonTypeInfo base type without a current
PolymorphicTypeValidator — and the 2026 bypass that mattered, where the validator
checked only the raw container class and never the nested generic type
parameters (fixed in 2.18.8 / 2.21.4 / 3.1.4), which is why "a validator is
present" is not the check, "the validator is current" is; XXE per parser factory,
because hardening DocumentBuilderFactory does not harden SAXParserFactory,
XMLInputFactory, TransformerFactory, SchemaFactory, Validator, JAXB or XPath;
JNDI lookup on untrusted input; ZipSlip; path traversal; command construction by
concatenation; java.util.Random where unpredictability is required.

State clearly which of these core SpotBugs covers and which need find-sec-bugs,
because teams assume the former.

DECIDE: (a) the MUST list, and whether it lives in the java-quality index
(always loaded) or only in the depth file; (b) whether Oracle's Secure Coding
Guidelines section 9 (Access Control) may be cited at all, given JEP 486 removed
the mechanism it describes in JDK 24 — the answer shapes how the file cites its
own sources; (c) whether the OCX SDK, which parses JSON from a subprocess it
launched, is inside or outside the untrusted-input boundary, and say why.

wave3_staged.group_label: Java runtime safety: untrusted input and failure handling
wave3_staged.label: Failures that vanish, and resources that do not close
wave3_staged.brief:
Write the error-handling and resource rows, which is where the highest-frequency
agent mistakes live and where several checks exist but are off by default.

Fetch, primary only: errorprone.info/bugpatterns pages for
InterruptedInCatchBlock, TryFailThrowable, UnusedException, CatchingUnchecked,
MustBeClosedChecker, StreamResourceLeak; spotbugs messages.xml entries for
OS_OPEN_STREAM, UL_UNRELEASED_LOCK, RV_RETURN_VALUE_IGNORED, DE_MIGHT_IGNORE,
REC_CATCH_EXCEPTION, SE_NO_SERIALVERSIONID; rules.sonarsource.com/java for
S2142, S1181, S4507 (and the deprecated S1148 it supersedes), S2095, S2057;
the Effective Java item list for items 69-77; openjdk.org/jeps/421.

Pin down which of these fire by default and which do not — this is the dive's
main value. CatchingUnchecked and UnusedException are in Error Prone's
DISABLED_CHECKS, meaning the single most characteristic pattern in
agent-written Java (wrap risky code in try/catch, log or ignore) is silent in
every default configuration measured. Establish the exact enabling syntax and
whether promoting them produces tolerable noise on a real codebase.

Cover: swallowed InterruptedException without re-interrupt; catch(Throwable);
try-with-resources including Files.walk/list/lines; ExecutorService shutdown on
every path; exception chaining and the new X(e.getMessage()) shape that drops the
cause; checked-versus-unchecked selection; System.exit() in library code;
printStackTrace over the logger; finalize() versus Cleaner; and
serialVersionUID on a Serializable class.

DECIDE: (a) the five rows that go in the index because they must be true in
every edit, and everything else that stays in the depth file; (b) whether the
three tools that all claim resource-leak detection (SonarJava S2095, PMD
CloseResource, Error Prone MustBeClosedChecker) get named individually or
whether the rule names one gate; (c) whether the sneaky-throw question — Goetz
calls the workarounds irresponsible, Kabutz documents the mechanics as a
pragmatic escape hatch — gets a rule or is recorded as contested with both
positions stated.
